transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Ava Reynolds (Redwood Solutions), Eleanor Zhang (Pinnacle), Tariq Malik (Pinnacle), Luis Ortega (Pinnacle)
Links shared: partner deck (placeholder): https://redwood.ai/partners/pinnacle-deck, initial benchmark template (redwood/shared)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today; quick intros from our side, I'm Sofia, AE for partners, um, Marcus is our SE who will lead the technical stuff, and Ava on solutions.
[00:14] Eleanor (Pinnacle): thanks Sofia, hi all, Eleanor here, head of partnerships at Pinnacle GPU, with Tariq our cloud ops lead and Luis on biz dev, excited to explore how we might work together.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood): hey, quick note, I'll mostly be asking about your infra, peering, and what a pilot looks like, but also happy to talk kernels and quantization, um, if that's useful.
[00:45] Tariq (Pinnacle): great; big picture for us: we resell GPU infra and we want close integrations with inference platforms, customers keep asking for turnkey LLM answers, so partner integrations that lower friction are high priority.
[01:10] Sofia: good, that's helpful. can you give a bit more on Pinnacle's typical customer profile and deployment models — public cloud like bare metal, or do you do colocation and cloud regions?
[01:30] Luis (Pinnacle): mostly hyperscaler resell + our managed bare-metal in three regions; we also do colo for enterprise. clients range from startups doing R&D to large finance shops doing private deployments.
[01:50] Sofia: ok that maps to a few of our customers. on Redwood side we have hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for partners, resell and tech integrations both possible — we usually start with a pilot on Dedicated or Private depending on data requirements.
[02:10] Eleanor: for us, channel economics matter. do you have standard reseller margins or is it bespoke per partner? and how do you handle crediting usage?
[02:30] Ava (Redwood): generally we have program tiers — quick overview: referral -> co-sell -> reseller. margins and commercial terms are dependent on commitment and region; we can send the partner program doc.
[02:45] Luis: makes sense. from a tech perspective Tariq here has questions about network peering and VPC connectivity for Private deployments.
[03:00] Tariq: yes, two things: 1) can Redwood run inside a customer's VPC, and what's required for peering? 2) how do you handle KMS/keys for encryption at rest?
[03:20] Marcus: we support Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane and options for VPC peering or private links; KMS integration (customer-managed) is supported — we integrate with common KMS/HSM and can surface audit logs. there are some ops assumptions for networking and firewall rules, but it's pretty standard.
[03:45] Tariq: any blockers for our bare-metal customers who don't want cloud APIs touching their infra?
[04:00] Marcus: we have an on-prem package for air-gapped or regulated workloads; it requires a bit more setup — things like model updates via signed artifacts, local KMS or HSM integration. in practice we run a private control plane or sometimes a hybrid depending on the customer's constraints.
[04:20] Eleanor: great — security is crucial. do you have SOC2 or ISO certs? customers will ask.
[04:30] Ava: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we can share the security pack and SOC2 report under NDA. we also support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and detailed audit logs per token/route.
[04:50] Luis: good. next, performance: customers want guaranteed latency. what's your typical latency on a 40B model on an A100 or H100 node?
[05:10] Marcus: ok quick note — numbers vary a lot by sequence length and batching. ballpark, for a single A100 with optimized runtime and quantization, 512 tokens with a good batch pipeline we see x ms per token, um, sorry I'll be less fuzzy — 50 to 120ms per token depending on setup; we should run a benchmark for your target workload.
[05:45] Tariq: can Redwood run on our custom kernels or only on mainstream ones? some of our infra uses custom compilers.
[06:00] Marcus: we ship a runtime that picks optimized kernels and has quantization-friendly paths; for really custom compilers we can evaluate compatibility, but typically customers use our runtime with pinned kernels; we also have suggestions for compilation and kernel selection that improve throughput.
[06:20] Eleanor: curious about billing/observability for partner customers — do we see per-token breakdowns or do we resell blocks?
[06:35] Ava: yes both — the console shows per-route/per-model token-level cost and latency breakdown, and for Dedicated we do capacity-based contracts with monitoring. for reseller flows we can integrate metering into your billing via usage reports or API.
[06:55] Luis: any references or partners you currently work with for integration in EMEA?
[07:05] Sofia: we have partners in EU and NA, happy to introduce — but first we'd like to understand the integration surface and the pilot scope.
[07:20] Marcus: if it's ok I'll jump into technical items I'm hearing: VPC peering, private deployment packaging, on-prem airgap, KMS/HSM, audit logs, and benchmarks for A100/H100. also caching — we support prefix/KV cache and continuous batching to reduce costs.
[07:45] Tariq: KV cache is important for a lot of inference workloads with token reuse. how is cache invalidation handled?
[08:00] Marcus: cache invalidation policies are configurable; we support TTLs and versioning per model so when you push new model variants you can invalidate prefixes or do staged rollouts.
[08:15] Eleanor: on the GTM side, would Redwood require exclusive partners in certain regions or verticals?
[08:30] Sofia: no hard exclusivity by default; we do strategic plays based on partner motion — if there's a go-to-market commitment (bookings targets) we can discuss preferential treatment or dedicated resources.
[08:50] Luis: commercial asks: do you have example reseller agreements and a starter MOU?
[09:05] Ava: yes we'll share a partner MOU and a reseller term sheet; legal will iterate once we see target volumes.
[09:20] Sofia: back to pilot—what would success look like for Pinnacle?
[09:30] Eleanor: piloting ease of deployment for a typical enterprise customer, 2-3 target accounts, baseline perf numbers on our A100 offering, and a repeatable ops/hand-off playbook for customers.
[09:50] Sofia: perfect, that helps. timeline? how fast do you want to move?
[10:00] Luis: goal is to have a pilot with 1-2 customers by end of Q4, so ideally tech deep dive next week and benchmarks in the following two weeks.
[10:15] Marcus: we can target tech deep dive week of Sep 14 and baseline perf by Sep 27. I'll prepare a perf script and a benchmark template (I'll share link).
[10:30] Tariq: on benchmarks, will you need access to our infra or do you want us to provision a test cluster?
[10:45] Marcus: either works; easiest is we provide a benchmark template and you run it on a Pinnacle node, or we can run it on Redwood Dedicated with your model artifacts if you prefer. for customer privacy many prefer run-on-prem.
[11:05] Emma (Redwood - actually misattributed speaker  -> Ava): quick clarification, model artifacts — do you host customer models or do customers bring their own?
[11:20] Tariq: both, customers sometimes bring proprietary models.
[11:30] Marcus: we support both; for bring-your-own-model we have model onboarding and signing; for hosted models we maintain versioning and rollouts. note on quantization: we can recommend quantization profiles for different accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
[11:50] Eleanor: regulatory/residency asks — some customers require EU-only data residency and strict logs retention; do you support region locking?
[12:05] Ava: yes region locking and dedicated regional control planes are part of the Private offering. we can scope an EU-only Private or on-prem options.
[12:20] Luis: any customer stories for finance where auditability was key?
[12:30] Sofia: we have a finance customer case (anonymized) where we ran Private in a colo with HSM-backed KMS and provided per-request audit logs; we can share a redacted case study under NDA.
[12:50] Tariq: sounds good. operational question: what's your support model during pilot — do you provide an SE on-call?
[13:05] Ava: yes pilot SE support is included for joint runs; Dedicated/reserved customers get higher SLAs and an escalation path.
[13:20] Luis: how do rollouts work — can we do canaries and automatic fallback?
[13:35] Marcus: we support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to older model variants if perf/regressions occur. it's in the deployments layer.
[14:00] Eleanor: what about pricing parity for resell — do you provide volume discounts?
[14:12] Sofia: we do commit tiers for Dedicated and partner discounts for reseller agreements. specifics depend on commitments and region.
[14:30] Marcus: one more technical point — model kernels and sequence length: if your customers run longer contexts, resource profile changes; we need concrete workload shapes for accurate perf estimates.
[14:50] Tariq: yes mostly 2-4k token contexts for some LLM workloads, others are shorter. can you support long context efficiently?
[15:10] Marcus: we have optimizations for long context (KV cache management, attention optimizations) but costs scale; we should include a long-context case in the benchmark.
[15:35] Luis: ok, switching to enablement — what collateral will you provide for our sales engineers?
[15:45] Ava: partner enablement pack: integration checklist, demo scripts, reference architecture diagrams, and joint playbooks. we'll share a link.
[16:00] Eleanor: perfect. any blockers from your side to start a pilot?
[16:10] Sofia: none immediate; we'll need an MOU and basic SSO/SCIM setup for joint customers. legal can exchange NDA quickly.
[16:25] Marcus: technical deep dive agenda proposal: 1) infra/networking & VPC peering, 2) benchmark template and perf script walkthrough, 3) model onboarding and quantization guidance, 4) security/KMS/audit logs. 60-90 minutes recommended.
[16:50] Tariq: that works. can we get a pre-read for the technical deep dive?
[17:00] Marcus: yes I'll put together a pre-read and the benchmark template, link in calendar invite.
[17:15] Luis: curious about commercial flows — do you support direct reseller invoices to end customers or do partners bill and Redwood invoices partners?
[17:30] Sofia: both patterns are supported; common is partner-bills, Redwood invoices partner, but we can discuss gross/net deals.
[17:45] Eleanor: ok let's talk timeline again and assignments.
[18:00] Sofia: recap: Redwood will send partner deck, partner MOU/reseller term sheet, and a benchmark template. Marcus will own the technical deep dive and benchmark script. Pinnacle will share target accounts and confirm pilot customers. legal teams to exchange NDA/MOU.
[18:20] Tariq: agreed.
[18:35] Luis: quick note — we also have a channel program manager who will be involved; I'll intro them after this call.
[18:45] Sofia: great, thanks. last question: any competitive concerns we should know?
[19:00] Eleanor: some customers compare to Nvidia-hosted services and Lambda; they ask about performance and total cost of ownership.
[19:15] Marcus: understood — we'll run comparative metrics where possible, but benchmarking on your hardware is the single best indicator.
[19:35] Sofia: ok next steps we'll send the deck and schedule deep dive; thanks everyone.

[45:00] Meeting end (approx)
